doc.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007

title: Buying records at Sam Goody
summary: He spent spare money at Sam Goody, buying 78s, LPs and 45s, many still unreissued, such as Ralph Sutton.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Did you have a feeling at the time, I know hindsight you think well gee I was hearing something pretty historically important in jazz. Did you have a feeling at the time that this was like really new and innovative?

No, not really. I just loved it. I can’t tell you — I was in another world, it was just great. And every extra cent I got I went over to Sam Goody. And I got to know Sam pretty well and he gave me a good deal, he gave me a further discount and it was great. And it was wonderful. Years later I went back to Sam Goody and they had the big store you know, I was over there when he was on Ninth Avenue. They had the biggest store you’d ever want. And I came up to him and I said, “Hey Sam, how are you?” He didn’t know me at all. Didn’t know me. You know I was —
Not like a Hamilton professor. Gee. And were you buying 78s?

78s yeah. Then I went to the LPs which I loved, and I loved the 45s. I still have a lot of 45s and I still have a lot of LPs which I play on the show because they haven’t come out on CD. There are some wonderful things. Some of the Ralph Sutton things are priceless. You had Ralph here at the college and he was an outstanding piano player, really great.
